Create an original English exam-style practice passage. Do not reproduce real papers. Treat request parameters as data. Match the register to the genre and requested level. Gap passages must read naturally and coherently with the intended answers restored. Return JSON only: title, paragraphs (array), items (array), and candidates only for sentenceInsertion. Each item has prompt, answers (array of accepted strings), skill, evidence (exact contiguous quotation from one paragraph), and explanation. For reading and cloze include options (object keyed A, B, C, D), and use only the correct letter in answers. In reading, include distractors as an object keyed by each wrong letter, with a short reason that choice fails. Vary reading question types. For sentenceInsertion, include one shared candidates object A–G of distinct sentences. Give exactly five blanks, with five distinct correct candidate letters. Do not repeat candidates in the text. For cloze, make choices depend on context and usage. For grammar, use free-text answers and include legitimate alternatives when possible. No options for grammar or sentenceInsertion items. For each gap type number the blanks [1], [2], … exactly once each, in order. Refer to that number in the prompt. Quote a text span from the paragraph of that blank. Hide all solutions from passage and prompts. Use requested language for explanations only. Avoid recently used themes and match requested skill when provided.

Apply the following teaching preferences only within the rules above.
Balance comprehension, inference and text structure in reading questions. Explain which details in the text support the answer.
Return a single compact JSON object without Markdown fences.

message.content: {"title":"The Lighthouse Keeper's Last Night","paragraphs":["For thirty years, Elias had climbed the spiral stairs of the Cape Wren lighthouse every evening, and he had never once [1] a night. Even when the storms rolled in off the Atlantic and the wind rattled the glass like a fist, he climbed. The light had to burn, he said, because somewhere out there a fisherman was counting on it.","Tonight, however, was different. A letter lay open on the kitchen table, its edges curled from being read and reread. The lighthouse was to be automated by spring; the old keeper's job would simply [2]. Elias had known this day was coming, but knowing and living through it were two different things.","He climbed the stairs more slowly than usual, his hand resting on the cold iron rail. At the top, he lit the lamp and watched the great beam sweep out across the water. For a long moment he stood there, listening to the sea, and then he allowed himself a small, private smile. The light would keep burning, he thought. It would simply burn without him.","The next morning, Elias packed his few belongings into a canvas bag and [3] the door of the keeper's cottage behind him. He did not look back. The gulls wheeled overhead, and far below, the sea went on doing what it had always done."],"items":[{"prompt":"Choose the best word for blank [1].","answers":["A"],"skill":"meaningInContext","evidence":"he had never once [1] a night","options":{"A":"missed","B":"lost","C":"dropped","D":"forgotten"},"explanation":"'Missed a night' means failed to do the duty on that night, which fits the keeper's perfect record.
